A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Spatial Reasoning Models work. Text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including Appendices A–G in v1 and A–H in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on MNIST Sudoku, Even Pixels, and Counting Polygons FFHQ, including sampling comparisons and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds Counting Stars results, architecture and noise-schedule ablations, classifier validation, and LLM Sudoku evaluations.

M1.justification: Appendix G adds an implemented DiT-B denoiser variant alongside the original UNet, a limited architectural extension. The SRM objectives, recursive noise-level sampler, uncertainty prediction, and generation-order algorithms remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The original three benchmark families remain. v2 adds Counting Stars FFHQ with 2–9 star points and textual Sudoku completion for LLMs in Appendix H. These extend input conditions and modalities within the existing counting and Sudoku tasks.

E2.justification: Table 10 introduces GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, and Phi-4 comparisons with trained SRM and diffusion models; Appendix H also reports qualitative DeepSeek-R1 evaluation. This adds a substantially different comparator family while retaining the original diffusion and discrete-oracle comparisons. The paper explicitly acknowledges the unequal training and modality conditions.

E3.justification: New protocols include DiT and cosine-schedule controls, object-consistency scoring, and three-shot textual Sudoku with format-based resampling and separate validity/consistency metrics. Appendix E.2 revises evaluator training from no enforced digit/count agreement to dropping that constraint in 50% of cases; whether earlier evaluations were rerun is unstated. The original 1,000-network-evaluation budget is retained.

E4.justification: Tables 8–9 add architecture and noise-schedule ablations. The stars experiment tests the frequency-based explanation for sequentialization benefits, while Figure 11 analyzes LLM errors across masking levels. Appendix H additionally discusses unsuccessful chain-of-thought and DeepSeek-R1 attempts. Earlier overlap, stochasticity, and sharpness analyses remain.

E5.justification: The new Figure 11 displays shaded bands around LLM performance curves, adding uncertainty-style reporting absent from v1's empirical plots. Their statistical meaning and calculation are unspecified, and neither version reports seeds or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: Original headline scores remain numerically unchanged, but substantial results are added. Table 3 reports stars accuracy of 0.150 for predicted order with overlap versus 0.070 for diffusion, plus object-consistency scores. Tables 8–9 add DiT and cosine results, Table 10 adds LLM accuracies, and Appendix E reports classifier validation accuracy above 99.9%. These are additional conditions and findings, not improvements to the original same-setting scores.

T1.justification: The core equations, reverse-process derivations and proofs, graph-order formulation, and recursive allocation algorithm in Appendices A–C are unchanged. The added experiments introduce no new formal theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract and introductory contribution list retain the same framework, training sampler, sequentialization, and benchmark claims. The conclusion's added emphasis on architecture and denoising-formulation independence restates properties already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 substantially develops the existing frequency-based explanation into an account of when objects and digits become committed during generation. Appendix G adds an interpretation of cosine-schedule performance, and Appendix H discusses LLM failures and comparison limitations. Section 3.1 also newly states that SRMs provide sampling rather than explicit probability representations.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies rectified flows as the main experimental schedule, specifies DiT-B's patch size of 7 and 130M parameters, extends dataset/evaluator details to stars, and supplies an LLM prompt example and retry instructions. Existing UNet hyperparameters and code/data access statements are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Peebles and Xie's diffusion-transformer reference and broadens the belief-propagation analogy from Bayesian networks to probabilistic graphical models. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to Diffusion Forcing and MAR remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, main section order, and most method exposition are preserved. Changes include localized terminology and caption edits, expanded experimental explanations, and the added Appendix H, without extensive rewriting of the existing document.

P2.justification: Table 3 expands from one accuracy column to grouped polygon/star accuracy and consistency columns. v2 adds Tables 8–10 and the three-panel Figure 11, updates Figure 5 with star examples, and relocates Tables 2–3. The principal existing diagrams and appendix mathematical displays are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the retained work through architecture and schedule checks in Tables 8–9, the stars consistency analysis, and newly reported validation of the counting classifiers. These provide useful evidence for generality and evaluation reliability. The explicitly unequal LLM comparison and undefined Figure 11 bands limit the additional conclusions, yielding a modest net quality improvement.
